description: Ansys STK (Systems Tool Kit) is a physics-based, time-dynamic modelling environment for analysing platforms and payloads such as satellites, aircraft, ground stations and sensors in a realistic mission context. It propagates orbits and trajectories (with Astrogator for mission design), analyses conjunctions and collision threats, computes coverage with custom figures of merit, and models communications link budgets and RF environments, radar and electro-optical sensors, with add-ons such as the RF Channel Modeler and Aviator. It was developed by Analytical Graphics Inc. (AGI), acquired by Ansys, and is now distributed by Ansys within Synopsys. Coverage: global and space-wide, from Earth's surface to deep space, with user-set time steps. Format and access: Windows desktop software in editions from a baseline STK to Pro, Premium Air, Premium Space and Enterprise, plus STK Engine for building applications through Python, MATLAB, Java, .NET and C/C++ APIs; paid under proprietary licences, while the baseline edition has historically been available free of charge after registration. Caveats: advanced capabilities need costly licences; results depend on the fidelity of the models and ephemerides that are loaded. Simulation uses: coverage and hazard exposure of satellite communication and navigation systems, capacity planning of constellations and ground networks, space-weather and interference studies, and mission digital twins. Related records: GMAT and Orekit are open alternatives for orbit analysis, and CelesTrak and Space-Track provide orbital element data.
